scope_guard.interpretation: Measuring product formation in a controlled enzyme assay is distinct from fitting enzyme parameters to a culture product endpoint. The former can establish assay activity when its denominator and timing are specified; it is not automatically kcat. This curation does not restore or claim fresh validation on an already scored product set.

evidence_grade_definitions.measured_extract_assay: Direct substrate/product experiment in a protein extract, normalized as reported; not necessarily a purified-enzyme initial rate.
evidence_grade_definitions.derived_unit_conversion: Arithmetic conversion of reported assay units, without adding biological assumptions about active enzyme fraction.
evidence_grade_definitions.primary_abstract_functional_complementat: Primary authors report gene-dependent chemical conversion in a heterologous cell. Function is supported, but purification, intrinsic kinetic constants and electron stoichiometry are not established by this readout.
evidence_grade_definitions.measured_protein_detection: Protein/peptide detection independent of product titers. Relative band intensity or peptide coverage is not absolute active-enzyme mass.
evidence_grade_definitions.reviewed_functional_annotation: Reviewed annotation with experimental provenance; the underlying experiment and its scope still determine what was measured.
evidence_grade_definitions.automated_annotation: Computational/automatic annotation, not a biochemical experiment.
evidence_grade_definitions.measured_comparator_only: A primary biochemical measurement for a different organism/protein; explicitly excluded from fungal numerical inputs.
evidence_grade_definitions.unresolved: Not established in the sources inspected. Null means unknown, not zero or absent.

quantitative_fungal_candidates.accession_mapping: The primary paper links crtE to DQ012943.1 and constructs pET28-ccrtE from sequenced cDNA of this strain. ENA links that genomic CDS to AAY33921.1. No sequence equality to the selected engineered strains is asserted.
quantitative_fungal_candidates.expression_host_and_construct: E. coli BL21-Gold (DE3), induced BL21+crtE carrying pET28-ccrtE

quantitative_fungal_candidates.unit_definition: Methods s2j defines 1 U as 1 micromole product formed per minute under the assay conditions; denominator is mg protein extract.

converted_value.calculation: The displayed column is (U/mg) multiplied by 10^6. Divide its numerical value by 10^6 to recover U/mg; multiply micromoles by 10^6 to express pmoles.
converted_value.qualification: This follows the printed heading and the stated U definition only. Raw counts and an initial-rate time course were not supplied in the inspected text for independent rederivation; do not silently reinterpret the small rate or its scale.

quantitative_fungal_candidates.assay_readout: 14C-IPP incorporation into acid-hydrolysable allylic prenyl products, hexane extraction and liquid-scintillation counting; RP-TLC of derived prenyl alcohols identifies the C20 product fraction. Table 3 reports the FPP-fed BL21+crtE assay product as C20. This is direct enzyme-assay product formation, not a culture carotenoid endpoint.

substrates.qualification: Called saturating in Methods s2j; no FPP saturation curve or Km is reported in these inspected sections.

substrates.name: 14C-IPP
substrates.qualification: Protocol lists labeled IPP and 20.2 micromolar IPP separately; preserve that recipe rather than silently changing the substrate concentration.

quantitative_fungal_candidates.redox_partner_note: CrtE prenyl transfer is not the unresolved CrtI desaturation. No terminal-electron-acceptor experiment is provided by this assay. DTT in the buffer is an assay additive, not a demonstrated CrtI electron donor/acceptor.
quantitative_fungal_candidates.pH_qualification: Methods s2j specifies 50 mM MOPS but not an explicit assay pH. E. coli extraction buffer is MOPS pH 7.5 in s2i; extraction pH is not silently promoted to a separately measured assay pH.

other_assay_conditions.not_enzyme_assay_temperature: The subsequent acid-hydrolysis step is 37 C for 1 h; it must not be mistaken for the enzyme incubation temperature.

what_it_establishes: A protein extract expressing this fungal CrtE catalyzes FPP plus IPP conversion to a C20 prenyl product under the stated conditions.
The primary experiment supplies an extract-normalized average activity and an assay design useful for independent follow-up.
what_it_does_not_establish: Intrinsic kcat, because CrtE mass and active fraction in the extract are unknown.
A validated initial rate or Vmax, because the inspected protocol uses one 60-minute incubation and does not establish time linearity, depletion or product inhibition.
Km, because a substrate concentration described as saturating is not a measured saturation curve.
Activity per biomass or active enzyme abundance in CEN.PK2-1c-derived strains.
A mandatory Mg2+ stoichiometry or metal dependence: including MgCl2 is not a cofactor-titration experiment.
transfer_limitations: Different donor strain/possible sequence, expression host, promoter, extraction and assay environment.
Soluble-extract recovery and host background activities are not accounted for by target gene copy counts.
A sequence-predicted molecular weight cannot convert a rate per mg mixed extract into kcat.
The assay's substrate/product detection supports CrtE function but does not quantify target in vivo allocation.

Several FPP-fed products were below TLC detection; the overexpressing extract contained a mixture of labeled products. These values were not promoted to pure CrtE rates or target enzyme abundance.

functional_and_protein_evidence.enzyme: Bifunctional phytoene synthase / lycopene beta-cyclase CrtYB
coordinates: Q7Z859 CATALYTIC ACTIVITY entries RHEA:34475, RHEA:32219 and RHEA:32239; ECO:0000269 / PMID:10589832
functional_and_protein_evidence.assay_readout: Expression/complementation in different carotenogenic E. coli strains and deletion derivatives identifies both functions and their domain association.
functional_and_protein_evidence.purification_or_abundance_basis: Functional expression/deletion studies in the accessible primary abstract; no purified CrtYB dose or kinetic normalization established
functional_and_protein_evidence.what_it_establishes: The expressed CrtYB identity entails an upstream synthase function and a downstream lycopene-consuming cyclase function; a standalone CrtB or terminal lycopene-only pathway is not an adequate biological description.
what_it_does_not_establish: A nonzero consumption floor under every target condition.
Cyclase Km/kcat, a synthase-to-cyclase activity ratio, a branch partition fraction or inhibition constant.
Mutually exclusive catalysis of the two domains or a measured common-enzyme occupancy constraint.
In vivo compartment-specific lycopene accessibility or enzyme mass.
functional_and_protein_evidence.product_readout_qualification: Product identity/complementation establishes function. No amount-based kinetic fit or numerical flux partition is made.
transfer_limitations: Functional evidence is not a quantitative branch competition assay

functional_and_protein_evidence.accession_qualification: The primary Methods identify the pYEplac195 CRTYB/CRTI/CRTE template and describe sequence verification; exact supplementary construct sequences were not inspected. Q7Z859/O13506/AAY33921.1 must not be silently equated with these tagged/fused constructs.
functional_and_protein_evidence.expression_host: S. cerevisiae BY4741-derived yHR21 strains; GAL80 deletion, GAL1-GAL10 expression system and tHMG1/CrtE background
functional_and_protein_evidence.assay_readout: Tagged-protein Western blots of normalized cell extracts, and in-gel trypsin digestion followed by LC-MS/MS peptide identification (GeLC-MS)
functional_and_protein_evidence.protein_purification_and_abundance_basis: Cell lysates and excised SDS-PAGE regions, not purified active protein. Western preparations normalize starting cells by OD600; the GeLC-MS protocol specifies crude-lysate loading and peptide identification, not absolute isotope-standard quantitation of active enzyme.
functional_and_protein_evidence.temperature_pH_qualification: No catalytic reaction temperature/pH applies to this denaturing protein-detection assay. Culture temperature/pH are not supplied here as transferable kinetic conditions.
observations: Natural CrtYB is detected by Western blot. CrtI detection depends on coexpression/construct context, and some bands are only tentatively assigned as truncation products.

GeLC-MS detects peptides supporting CrtI and the synthase portion of natural CrtYB; separate CrtE peptides are detected in the analyzed yeast extracts. Peptides also support the engineered tridomain fusion.
The authors explicitly characterize Western information as semi-quantitative. Peptide coverage and apparent gel molecular mass are identity/detection evidence, not an active-enzyme mass fraction.
The experimental host is BY4741-derived. A CEN.PK113-7D sequence database used for peptide searching in Methods 2.7 is not evidence that the experimental cells were CEN.PK2-1c.
functional_and_protein_evidence.localization_limit: No organelle fractionation or live-cell colocalization measurement was established by these inspected experiments. The discussion extrapolates from bacterial/plant membrane-association work; that extrapolation is not measured fungal localization. Similarly, Q7Z859 membrane annotations are predictive, not a demonstrated target compartment.
functional_and_protein_evidence.turnover_limit: A possible truncation band is not a measured degradation half-life. Failure to detect a hydrophobic domain is not proof of its absence.
transfer_limitations: Tagged/domain-fusion expression and batch harvest rather than the selected balanced-growth conditions
Extraction, blot transfer and peptide ionization bias
No calibrated protein amount, holoenzyme fraction or specific activity

functional_and_protein_evidence.conclusion: An automatic cofactor annotation is neither a measured terminal electron acceptor nor a stoichiometric NADH-production assay. It does not authorize the NAD hypothesis as strict chemistry, and does not resolve whether fungal CrtI contains catalytic FAD.

bacterial_comparison_not_fungal_inputs.enzyme: Pantoea ananatis CRTI-His6 expressed in E. coli JM109
bacterial_comparison_not_fungal_inputs.accession_qualification: The primary experiment is identified by its organism and described construct. An exact accession-to-assayed-sequence match was not established here. The separately inspected P21685 record is labeled Pantoea ananas / Erwinia uredovora and is not asserted to be the selected fungal enzyme.
bacterial_comparison_not_fungal_inputs.purification: Soluble bacterial expression fraction, immobilized-metal affinity chromatography followed by gel permeation; near homogeneity. Protein estimated by Bradford. Mainly apoenzyme was recovered before reconstitution.

activity_and_cofactor_findings.finding: Purified bacterial CRTI desaturates liposomal 15-cis-phytoene to all-trans-lycopene when FAD is supplied. LC-MS/MS detects FAD with traces of FMN in the isolated material; NAD(H)/NADP(H) analyses yield no signals. This does not establish fungal cofactor occupancy or exclude fungal NAD coupling.

Desaturation is inactive under nitrogen without an alternative acceptor despite excess oxidized FAD. Oxygen consumption accompanies conversion under aerobic conditions. This supports oxygen as an acceptor for this bacterial assay, not an identified fungal terminal pair.

Reconstitution with FAD during membrane association yields active material after removal of free FAD. Protein associated without FAD is inactive and is not rescued by subsequently adding FAD. This supports a structural/catalytic bound-flavin role and argues against freely exchanging FAD/FADH2 as a net catalytic-cycle electron sink for this comparator.

Quinones including duroquinone and Q10 support anaerobic activity in the in vitro lipid system. The paper raises respiratory-chain coupling as a question. This does not prove Q6 access, mitochondrial localization or electron transfer for the fungal construct.

oxygen_product_identification_experiment.assay_readout: Oxygen electrode plus quantified lycopene formation in an upscaled liposome assay; response of oxygen-consumption kinetics to added superoxide dismutase and catalase

oxygen_product_identification_experiment.condition_qualification: s4d gives the standard phosphate-buffer/liposome assay at 37 C and pH 8.0 with FAD. The upscaled oxygen paragraph explicitly changes volume and enzyme/substrate doses; a complete separate upscaled buffer/FAD recipe is not reported there, so those standard conditions are not represented as a newly verified upscaled recipe.

oxygen_product_identification_experiment.product_amount_derivation_kind: Direct in vitro redox accounting with independently measured oxygen uptake; not culture endpoint fitting

unresolved.quantity: Exact engineered CrtE/CrtYB/CrtI sequences and targeting/tag/isoform changes
Intrinsic CrtE kcat and Km for FPP and IPP under relevant conditions
CrtYB synthase and both cyclization-step kcat/Km; simultaneous-domain occupancy and substrate/product competition
Fungal CrtI initial-rate kinetics, intermediate specificity and electron-coupling mechanism
Fungal CrtI catalytic FAD binding/occupancy and free-flavin exchange on the turnover timescale
Absolute enzyme amount, active fraction and accessible membrane/compartment in the selected host/conditions
Lycopene synthesis, cyclase consumption, degradation/sequestration and growth-dilution contributions separately

identifiability_and_conversion_rules.pool_balance: For intracellular lycopene amount L normalized to biomass, dL/dt = v_synthesis - v_consumption - mu*L; add an explicit loss term if oxidation/export is material. Rates and time units must be consistent.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.steady_state: dL/dt = 0 identifies only v_synthesis - v_consumption = mu*L if other losses are absent. It does not identify either flux alone.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.nonidentifiability: For any admissible g(t), replacing v_synthesis by v_synthesis+g(t) and v_consumption by v_consumption+g(t) leaves the same pool trajectory. Even a dense L(t) series is insufficient without another flux-sensitive readout or a separately verified perturbation.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.minimal_extra_information: Independently identify one flux, or observe labeled formation and disappearance with upstream input and downstream products in a mass-balanced time course. Measure dilution independently and test additional losses rather than absorbing them into a product-specific multiplier.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.enzyme_capacity: Only after compatible kcat and enzyme amount are available can v_max = kcat*E_active be formed. With kcat in s^-1 and E_active in mmol/gDW, multiply by 3600 for mmol/gDW/h. If only total enzyme is known, unknown active fraction makes that capacity an optimistic bound, not realized flux.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.specific_activity_to_kcat: For a saturated, linear assay expressed as A micromol min^-1 mg^-1 of pure enzyme, molecular mass M g/mol gives kcat = A*M/60000 s^-1 per polypeptide when one active site per polypeptide is independently appropriate. Correct the site convention, purity and active fraction explicitly. This conversion is NOT valid for the 2014 total-extract denominator without measured CrtE fraction and active-site basis.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.reaction_counting: Define whether an event is one phytoene molecule made, one lycopene molecule formed, one desaturation or one ring closure. Two GGPP per phytoene, four desaturations per phytoene-to-lycopene conversion, and two cyclization steps must not be mixed into an unlabelled kcat conversion.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.bifunctional_protein_accounting: CrtYB is one polypeptide carrying two functional domains. Do not charge its mass twice as if synthase and cyclase were independently expressed proteins. Separate per-domain capacity inequalities may refer to the same measured CrtYB pool; an additive occupancy constraint or fixed activity partition requires evidence that simultaneous catalysis is excluded. Mere bifunctionality does not establish that exclusion.
identifiability_and_conversion_rules.intermediate_relaxation: Omitting downstream consumption can define a relaxed intermediate-capacity bound; it cannot be called a realized content prediction. Conversely, functional annotation alone cannot justify an arbitrary positive cyclase flux floor.

minimal_independent_evidence_plan.objective: Identify the actual proteins and independently measure their amounts and location.
minimal_measurements: Obtain the actual amino-acid sequences/construct maps, including tags, domain mutations, isoforms and targeting additions, without opening product outcomes. Match to the literature proteins explicitly.

Use isotope-dilution targeted LC-MS/MS with distinguishable proteotypic peptides and recovery controls, or calibrated immunoblots with purified standards, for absolute CrtE, CrtYB and CrtI amount per gDW in independently specified conditions. Include peptides from both CrtYB domains and intact-size checks.

Measure soluble/membrane partition and compartment access with marker-controlled fractionation and/or validated imaging. Control tag effects and membrane extraction recovery; proximity is not proof of electron transfer.
Pair protein amount with independent activity recovery or active-site/cofactor occupancy measurements. Total expressed mass is not necessarily folded, assembled, active holoenzyme.
identifies: Absolute total enzyme and defensible active-fraction bounds
Accessible compartment rather than a presumed cytosolic/mitochondrial connection

minimal_independent_evidence_plan.objective: Measure substrate-controlled initial rates using actual fungal constructs, not culture endpoint fits.
minimal_measurements: Purify or quantitatively immunocapture active full-length CrtE, CrtI and CrtYB; quantify target purity and active-site basis. Retain required membrane/reconstitution context.

For CrtE, measure FPP + IPP conversion to chemically identified GGPP. Use several early time points, several enzyme doses, and a matrix of FPP and IPP concentrations. Verify linearity and substrate mass balance before estimating kcat/Km. The Alcaino assay is a methodological starting point, not the target parameter.

For CrtYB synthase, measure GGPP disappearance and phytoene appearance with the two-to-one substrate stoichiometry. For cyclase, supply independently quantified lycopene or gamma-carotene and resolve gamma- and beta-carotene formation separately.

For CrtI, resolve phytoene and desaturation intermediates as well as lycopene over early time points; identify any extra products before assigning a single event rate. Couple rate measurements to P3 rather than silently assuming an acceptor.

Report pH, temperature, salt, lipid composition, accessible substrate activity, purification, oligomer/site convention, cofactors, error model and replicates. Membrane-associated apparent Km is not automatically a bulk intracellular concentration constant.
identifies: Intrinsic/apparent kinetics with a declared assay context
Specific activity with a valid pure-enzyme conversion
does_not_identify_alone: Target in vivo active protein amount

minimal_independent_evidence_plan.objective: Resolve the actual fungal electron acceptor, released reduction product and catalytic flavin role before strict chemistry installation.
minimal_measurements: Use purified sequence-matched fungal CrtI in a defined membrane/substrate system with no-enzyme, heat-inactivated, no-substrate, no-cofactor and contaminating-activity controls.

Compare aerobic and rigorously anaerobic turnover with explicitly supplied candidate acceptors. Measure acceptor reduction directly, not just carotenoid appearance: oxygen uptake, NADH/NADPH or reduced quinone as appropriate. Do not assume host quinone access from a cell-free reaction.

Quantify released peroxide with validated recovery and orthogonal detection; test superoxide and lipid oxidation with interference controls. SOD/catalase effects or their absence are insufficient to identify water. If water is claimed, use suitable isotope/product analysis or complete electron/product accounting that discriminates direct enzyme chemistry from a composite detoxification route.

Close an electron balance against chemically identified carotenoid conversions and any oxidized lipids/other sinks. A phytoene-to-lycopene conversion removes eight hydrogen atoms, but that arithmetic does not identify the acceptor or product.

Measure bound flavin identity and occupancy by spectroscopy/LC-MS after separation of free cofactor. Test apo/holo reconstitution, washout and redox cycling, and free-FAD exchange relative to turnover. Do not represent catalytic FAD as a stoichiometrically consumed free pool.

If activity requires a host redox partner or membrane fraction, identify that partner and demonstrate physical access/coupling in the selected yeast compartment before introducing an overall reaction.
identifies: A specific supported terminal pair and stoichiometry, or continued ambiguity
Whether a composite partner-dependent mechanism is required
does_not_identify_alone: In vivo flux or enzyme allocation
A capacity-favorable hypothesis as biologically true

minimal_independent_evidence_plan.objective: Test CrtYB's joint domain behavior and downstream substrate competition without inventing a partition multiplier.
minimal_measurements: At a fixed independently measured amount of intact CrtYB, assay synthase and cyclase separately and together in a factorial GGPP/lycopene/gamma-carotene design. Quantify both activities and test cross-substrate/product effects.

Vary the active CrtI:CrtYB ratio in a reconstituted fungal-enzyme system and follow the full intermediate panel over time. A changed intermediate fraction alone is not a measured individual enzyme rate.

Use branch-selective mutants only after verifying that the other activity, folding, abundance and localization are retained. A whole CrtYB deletion removes both synthesis and consumption and is not an isolated cyclase perturbation.
Determine whether domains can turn over concurrently. Fit only experimentally identifiable inhibition/occupancy terms; otherwise retain interval bounds and structural uncertainty.
identifies: Whether separate or joint domain constraints are appropriate
Downstream-consumption capability under a measured protein basis

minimal_independent_evidence_plan.objective: Separate intermediate synthesis, consumption and dilution with an independent perturbation or tracer experiment.
minimal_measurements: Measure biomass/growth dilution, phytoene, lycopene, gamma-carotene and beta-carotene amounts and isotopologues at multiple short time points, with extraction-recovery and membrane-pool controls.

One minimal route is a rapid, independently verified synthesis shutoff upstream of lycopene while retaining cyclase activity. During the validated shutoff interval, lycopene disappearance after correcting for growth dilution measures total removal; simultaneous downstream appearance separates cyclization from other loss. Confirm the perturbation does not directly alter CrtYB or pool accessibility.

An alternative is a pulse-chase with a measured input-label time course and both upstream and downstream labeling. Do not assume extracellular lycopene enters the relevant intracellular membrane pool; validate tracer access or label its intracellular precursor.

Measure or bound oxidation, export, storage-pool exchange and recovery loss rather than assigning all disappearance to cyclase. Multiple initial intermediate levels are needed to distinguish an effective first-order decay constant from saturable consumption.

Jointly analyze independent enzyme amounts/activities and these time courses. Reject models in which only v_synthesis-v_consumption is identifiable; retain separate flux intervals if the data cannot distinguish them.
identifies: Separate fluxes if the additional measurements/perturbation truly constrain them
Whether the assumed single pool is adequate
does_not_identify_alone: Both fluxes from an unperturbed lycopene pool trajectory

minimal_independent_evidence_plan.objective: Keep independent biochemical parameterization separate from validation of product predictions.
minimal_measurements: Freeze the enzyme-assay inputs, sequence-transfer rules, redox evidence status, uncertainty propagation and analysis before new product outcomes are inspected.

Use genuinely new, prespecified strains/conditions or experiments for prospective prediction assessment. The already scored product set remains retrospective/diagnostic and cannot become fresh validation after new evidence or model changes.
Do not choose a redox variant, active-enzyme fraction, compartment or branch partition by which value improves existing prediction scores.
identifies: Prospective predictive validity only if a new independent test is actually performed
does_not_identify_alone: A biochemical mechanism from prediction agreement

bounded_search_and_access_limits.search_scope: Prioritized the two original fungal gene papers, a primary fungal CrtE assay, a primary heterologous protein-detection study, and one primary bacterial redox comparator. Europe PMC searches rendered bibliographic metadata only; production studies were not harvested for fitted rates or product outcomes.

additional_verified_leads_not_used_as_qu.reason_not_used: Abstract concerns Neurospora al-2 functional specificity, not purified kinetics of the actual Phaffia enzymes. Its presence in a reviewed CrtYB reference list does not supply a fungal rate or competition constant.
Selected follow-up primary source identified from references; this XML endpoint returned no article. No kinetic or competition conclusion was inferred from the failed request.

Reviewed bacterial record is labeled Pantoea ananas / Erwinia uredovora; no reference entry for PMID 22745782 appeared in the inspected response. No exact assay-sequence link or fungal identity was inferred.

bounded_search_and_access_limits.availability_limit: The two 1999 fungal papers were accessible at abstract/annotation level, not full primary body. The repository OA flag for CrtI did not yield a manuscript. No paywall or access-control bypass, new dependency, or broad local filesystem search was used.
bounded_search_and_access_limits.absence_claim_limit: No compatible fungal CrtI/CrtYB kcat/Km, measured terminal acceptor/product pair, calibrated target active abundance or independently identifiable target consumption flux was established in the inspected material. This is a bounded evidence conclusion, not a claim of exhaustive literature absence.
